stem: A quality control inspector tests a production line by examining every 15th item after a random start between 1 and 15. From a batch of 300 items, how many items will be selected in the sample?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 15 is the sampling interval itself; confusing the interval with the resulting sample size gives this wrong answer.
In systematic sampling, sample size = population size / sampling interval = 300 / 15 = 20.
30 results from computing 300 / 10 instead of 300 / 15, using the wrong denominator.
45 results from computing 300 / 15 x 2.25 or erroneously using 300 / (15 - something), reflecting an arithmetic error in applying the formula.

explanation: Systematic sampling selects every k-th unit from a list of N units after a random start. The sample size n = N / k = 300 / 15 = 20.

explanation_sections.punchline: The setup decision is recognising that systematic sampling gives n = N/k; the calculation is then a single division: 300/15 = 20.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: systematic sampling with sampling interval k = 15. State the formula: n = N/k. Map the givens: N = 300, k = 15. Compute: n = 300/15 = 20.
explanation_sections.lesson: In systematic sampling, the sampling interval k = N/n; equivalently, n = N/k. Never confuse k (the interval) with n (the sample size).
explanation_sections.timing: 30 seconds. The trap is reading the question as 'how many items per group' and reporting 15 (the interval). Divide, do not report the divisor.
